- **Log files covering the window (disjoint, verified first/last timestamps):**
  `proxy.log.2026-10-27_10` (10:16:12→16:16:11), `proxy.log.2026-10-27_16`
  (16:16:13→22:16:12), `proxy.log-2026-10-28_00` (22:16:13→23:59:59),
  `proxy.log.2026-10-27_22` (00:00:02→04:16:11), `proxy.log.2026-10-28_04`
  (04:16:13→10:16:12), `proxy.log` (10:16:13→live).
- **Config at measurement:** `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio: 0.5`,
  `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens: 25000`, `local_prefill_deadline_seconds:
  120`, `local_admission_guard_budget_safety_fraction: 0.95`.
- **Code identity (shared checkout; tip moves without restart):** read at run
  time and recorded in the result comment.
- **Superseded history:** the `## Pinned measurement window (Q1 ...)` section
  below (2026-10-25T21:19 → 2026-10-26T21:19) and the 2026-10-26 re-arm
  (21:02 → 21:02) are retained as history only.

## Objective

Execute the **24 h post-deploy verification of AC4** for `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`
(resident-prefix admission + session tenancy) on a restart-free production
window and record whether **scheduling-attributed** `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
cancellations fell by **≥ 90 %** against that same window's own re-anchored
baseline — plus the AC5 observability and AC6 lease-watchdog checks.

This item only measures and reports; it changes no scheduling logic.

## Problem statement

The epic's AC4 cannot be verified inside the implementing session: it needs a
full 24 h production soak on code that is actually running. Verification also
silently invalidates itself — the proxy restarted **six times on 2026-10-25**
(log rotations at 11:01:54, 11:21:20, 11:46:48, 18:57:27, 20:16:58 and
21:18:04 UTC), and each restart resets the in-memory residency/lease state, so
a window that contains a restart measures nothing. Without a pinned window,
attested uptime, and a window-scoped baseline, the ≥ 90 % claim is
unfalsifiable.

## Users

- **Proxy operator** — needs a defensible verdict on the thrash change before
  the epic closes, and needs to know whether to roll back.
  - *As the proxy operator, I want the 24 h result stated with its window,
    counts and baseline, so I can accept the change or roll it back.*
- **Implementing agents of the epic** — need AC4 satisfied by an independent
  measurement, not by their own in-session numbers.
  - *As the epic's implementing agent, I want the verdict recorded on the epic,
    so I can close AC4 without self-certifying.*
- **Future thrash investigations** — need the measured window, the corrected
  commands and the classifier rule as precedent.
  - *As a future investigator, I want the procedure and its numbers in
    `findings.md`, so I do not re-derive the methodology.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Preconditions attested before measuring.** The result records: the
  proxy PID and its start instant (`ps -o lstart -p <pid>`), continuous uptime
  covering the entire window, the code identity read **from the checkout the
  running proxy was started from** (`git log -1 --format=%H` — the checkout is
  shared, so the tip moves without a restart), and explicit confirmation that
  both target changes are in that tree (`LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` ladder;
  `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` 25k cold budget / 120 s deadline).
- **AC2 — Window pinned and restart-free.** The window is
  `2026-10-31T00:42:00Z → 2026-11-01T00:42:00Z` (ISO-8601 UTC, exactly 24 h,
  start ≥ the latest proxy restart; **re-arm #4**, after three restarts inside
  re-arm #3 — `2026-10-30T23:10:49Z`, `2026-10-31T00:37:53Z` and
  `2026-10-31T00:41:57Z` — invalidated it; see the re-arm #4 section at the top
  and comment `LP-C0MVWC0Y8C002ZWBT`). Re-arm trail: #1 `2026-10-25T21:19Z`,
  #2 `2026-10-27T10:17Z`, #3 `2026-10-30T10:36Z` — all invalidated by in-window
  restarts; #4 is current.
  Restart-freedom is evidenced by `ps -o lstart` plus the absence of
  `Logging initialised … pid=` / `Rotated previous proxy log aside` lines
  between start and end. A restart inside the window re-arms the run (new
  window, both windows recorded) and never yields a PASS.
- **AC3 — Absolute counts recorded.** `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events and
  total wasted prefill tokens for the window, with the
  `LP-0MVODJ3P6000AIUM` caveat stated (event fields are recomputed post-hoc, so
  `wasted_prefill_tokens` is overstated; the figure is either re-derived from
  admission-side data or reported with that caveat).
- **AC4 — Scheduling-attributed split, reproducible.** Every deadline event is
  classified as scheduling-attributed when either (a) the `reuse_ratio` logged
  at admission was below `server.local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`
  (0.5 in `proxy/config.yaml`), or (b) `slot_owner_session` at admission
  differs from the owner at the deadline event. Per-class counts are recorded;
  the remainder is reported as genuine GPU-speed misses and declared out of
  scope. Because the event line logs only `session` and `deadline`
  (`proxy/proxy/router.py` ~line 1616), the classifier joins each event to the
  session's most recent `routing_resident_prefix` line and any `local_eviction*`
  line before it — the join rule is stated in the result, and events whose
  join is ambiguous are counted separately and **not** as scheduling-attributed
  (conservative).
- **AC5 — Baseline re-anchored to the same window.** Baseline is computed by
  capturing the window with `capture_prefill_thrash_window.py` and replaying it
  through the residency ladder with `replay_prefill_occupancy.py
  --window-fixture`, and the reduction percentage against the
  scheduling-attributed count is stated explicitly. The 2026-10-24 figures
  (160 events / 5.4 h ≈ 780k wasted prefill tokens) are historical reference
  only and are never the baseline.
- **AC6 — Verdict recorded with both gates.** **PASS** requires (i) ≥ 90 %
  reduction in scheduling-attributed cancellations and (ii) no
  `local_lease_active` refusal window longer than the 180 s watchdog bound. On
  FAIL the measured numbers are recorded, a `discovered-from` item is created
  with the offending log extract, and this item is not marked complete.
- **AC7 — Staged-rollout observability check.** The window's
  `analyze_proxy_usage.py` report contains `## Residency-aware admission` with
  the `residency_decisions` / `residency_resident_admits` /
  `residency_evicted_denials` / `residency_tenant_limit_denials` /
  `local_evictions` counters and the per-session slot-owner churn table. An
  absent section, or decisions logged but all unmeasured, is a finding (ladder
  not emitting), never a pass.
- **AC8 — Result recorded and propagated.** One structured result comment on
  this item (window bounds, precondition attestation, counts, classified split,
  baseline, reduction %, verdict), cross-referenced from
  `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` and from
  `Post-deploy 24 h prefill regression verification (LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I)`,
  which consumes the same report set (Q2 decision A) rather than running its
  own window.
- **AC9 — Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/slot-thrashing-investigation/findings.md`
  gains the measured window and verdict (and the corrected capture invocation
  with `--log`), so the 2026-10-24 numbers are labelled historical; all related
  documentation (code comments, README, docs site entries) is updated to
  reflect the changes.
- **AC10 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (executed
  via the test skill / dev-push gate; no ad-hoc full-suite runs).

## Constraints

- **No restart inside the window.** Evidence that this is the dominant risk:
  six restarts on 2026-10-25 alone; the 21:18:10 restart was
  `source=manual actor=unknown`. A restart resets residency/lease state and
  invalidates the run.
- **Do not run before the pinned instant, and do not peek early** in a way that
  biases the decision.
- **Read-only measurement:** no `start-proxy.sh --restart`, no config reload, no
  log truncation during the window. Rotated logs (`.gz`) are part of the
  window and must be passed to the capture tool.
- **Counters come from the analysis tool**, not ad-hoc `grep`
  (`LP-0MVOAQDB4002D56G` exposes first-class `--json` keys); `grep` is only used
  for the classification join and for spot evidence.
- **Baseline is window-scoped**, per AC5.
- Analysis window is given with explicit `--start`/`--end` (the
  `05:00 UTC`-boundary convention is a convenience, not a requirement of the
  tool — see Decisions (Q1).

## Existing state (evidence gathered 2026-10-25T23:20–23:35Z)

- **Latest proxy restart: 2026-10-25T21:18:10Z**, PID **3057415**
  (`ps -o lstart -p 3057415` → `Sun Oct 25 21:18:08 2026`; log head:
  `Logging initialised at /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log pid=3057415`
  followed by `Proxy restart attribution: source=manual actor=unknown`).
  ⇒ earliest legal run instant is **2026-10-27T21:02Z**; the item's previous
  instant (11:22Z) is stale.
- **Ladder is emitting:** 871 `routing_resident_prefix` decisions since the
  21:18:10 restart; corrected form present
  (`n_past_actual=none … reuse_ratio=none … residency_source=non_resident`).
- **23 `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events** since the restart (~2 h), all
  `deadline=120s`, e.g. `session=audit-SA-0MVO7XZAB0095R6F-phase2_deep-…` —
  audit sessions visibly dominate the sample, so the user/audit split matters.
- **Report section verified live** for 22:18–23:18: `## Residency-aware
  admission` renders — 446 residency decisions (0 measured / 446 unmeasured),
  9 `tenant_limit` denials, 16 `local_eviction` (8 `local_eviction_after_acceptance`,
  all `prefill_deadline`), 4 of 23 sessions with slot-owner churn.
- **Pipeline smoke-tested end to end** (22:30–23:00): capture → 430 attempts,
  1 deadline-cancelled, ~2152 wasted tokens modelled; replay → 421 over budget,
  9 admitted, **0 over-budget cold admissions**.
- **Gap found — the documented capture command is incomplete:** the item's
  re-anchoring snippet omits `--log`, which is required
  (`capture_prefill_thrash_window.py: error: the following arguments are
  required: --log`). Corrected form is used in this brief.
- **Gap found — classification needs a join:** `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
  logs only `session` + `deadline`, so rule (b) cannot be read off the event
  line itself; it must be joined per session (see AC4).
- **`local_lease_active` is observable**: 37 occurrences since the restart
  (e.g. `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue … queued_duration=60.00s
  reason=local_lease_active`), so the AC6 watchdog check is measurable.
- **Overlapping verification item exists:** `LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I` (Post-deploy
  24 h prefill regression verification, `plan_complete`, promoted to top level
  on 2026-10-25T22:23Z) measures the same change set with a different window
  (2026-10-25T20:17Z → 2026-10-26T20:17Z, code `fc3c6e2e`) and the historical
  fixture-restated baseline rather than a window-scoped re-anchoring. **That
  window is now invalid:** the 21:18:10 restart falls inside it. Two
  independent runs would produce two contradictory verdicts — see Open
  Question 2.
- **Armed origin:** this item was created and retitled by
  `LP-0MVN4LC7N005XH7P` (`completed`), whose AC4 (deliverable) requires this
  item to carry the deploy-derived instant, the pinned window, the
  re-anchoring query and the classifier.

## Desired change

Nothing in the scheduling path. This item produces:

1. A pinned, restart-free 24 h window recorded on the item **before** the run.
2. One measurement run of the usage analysis plus the re-anchored baseline
   replay, with the scheduling-attributed split applied.
3. A structured result comment with the PASS/FAIL verdict, propagated to the
   epic (and to `LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I` if it shares this run).
4. The corresponding `findings.md` entry, so the methodology and the numbers
   are reusable.

## Measurement commands (verified working 2026-10-25)

```bash
# 0. Preconditions (attest before measuring, AC1/AC2)
ps -o pid,lstart -p $(pgrep -f "uvicorn proxy.server:app" | head -1)
cd /home/rgardler/projects/llm && git log -1 --format='%H %ci'

# 1. Window report (AC3, AC6, AC7) — explicit window, first-class counters
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
  --start "2026-10-31 00:42:00" --end "2026-11-01 00:42:00" \
  --output-dir ~/proxy-usage-reports/ac4-rearm4 --json

# 2. Window-scoped baseline (AC5) — every log file overlapping the window,
#    incl. in-process rotations (proxy.log.YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS) and .gz
#    (window file set re-enumerated at run time — do NOT hard-code it)
python3 proxy/scripts/capture_prefill_thrash_window.py \
  --start "2026-10-31 00:42:00" --end "2026-11-01 00:42:00" \
  --log /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-31_00 \
  --log /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log \
  --out /tmp/ac4_window_rearm4.jsonl
python3 proxy/scripts/replay_prefill_occupancy.py x \
  --window-fixture /tmp/ac4_window.jsonl    # expects 0 over-budget cold admissions

# 3. Classifier join (AC4) — per-session decision before each deadline event
grep -E "prefill_deadline_exceeded|routing_resident_prefix|local_eviction" \
  /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log
```

## Pinned measurement window (Q1 — operator decision A, 2026-10-25)

- **Start:** `2026-10-25T21:19:00Z` (**already elapsed** — the binding
  restart-anchored freeze is therefore in effect immediately).
- **End / run instant:** `2026-10-26T21:19:00Z` — the analysis runs at/after
  this instant and covers the full 24 h.

`Post-deploy 24 h prefill regression verification
(LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I)` (**re-based by comment 2026-10-25**) consumes this
run's report for its waste/503/eviction-reason/rollback checks instead of
running a separate window. This item owns the scheduling-attributed

  re-run with a partially-reset window.

  decisions before its deadline event. Mitigation: use the latest decision

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the parent item's gating precondition verified from
measured evidence, so that prefill tuning only starts once local actually
carries sustained work.

## What the gate is

Parent **LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT** AC0 requires a comment recording a measured
**>60 % local (GPU) busy** night before any change is made. Busy is the
`## Local model utilization` upper bound (dispatch -> finish: prefill +
decode) from the deterministic `proxy-usage-analysis` CLI, over a complete
night window (22:00-07:00 local).

## Evidence at planning time (2026-10-25)

- Night **2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00**: busy **2.2 %** (719 s of
  32 400 s; 27 local streams; prefill 336 slot-s; decode 383 slot-s;
  idle 97.8 %).
  Command:
  `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "2026-10-23 22:00:00" --end "2026-10-24 07:00:00" --output-dir /tmp/wl-gate-check --json`
- Same night in the 24 h daily report (`~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`,
  window 2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52): busy 10.2 %.

**The gate is NOT met.** The parent is left `blocked` at stage
`plan_complete`, and every other child of this plan depends on this item, so
none of them is dispatchable until the gate passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0: The gate AC is satisfied - a comment on this item records the measured >60% GPU utilisation for a full night, from the usage-analysis report, before any change is made.
- AC1: A comment on the parent records local busy % for a **complete** night
  window (22:00-07:00), with the exact CLI invocation, the window bounds and
  the artifact directory used.
- AC2: The gate is declared met **only** when `busy_pct >= 60` for the whole
  night (`definition: dispatch_to_finish` in the CLI `--json` summary).
- AC3: When the gate is not met this item stays **open and incomplete** with
  the evidence comment (recorded `blocked` status is derived from dependency
  edges in `wl` and cannot be pinned, so this item is the lock: keeping it
  incomplete keeps every dependent child dependency-blocked), and no other
  child of the plan is started.
- AC6: This item must never be marked `completed` while the gate is unmet. If a
  run cannot leave it open, it records the evidence and files the deferral on
  the parent rather than completing the gate.
- AC4: When the gate is met this item completes with the evidence comment and
  the parent plus its dependent siblings are unblocked in the same update
  sequence.
- AC5: Measurement only - no configuration, flag or code change.

**Key Files:**
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` - deterministic report CLI
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` - report section definitions

## Dependencies

None. All other children of this plan depend on this item.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the A/B benchmark harness to produce valid measurements
in the **40-80k-token** band, because that is the band that produces the
multi-minute local first-byte tail and the only band in which a micro-batch
change can still help.

## Why

`docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md` (LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS) measured 8.9k / 17.9k
/ 26.8k prompts, found the ubatch 1024->2048 win confined to ~18k (memory
bandwidth bound above), and closed with: *"If this is revisited: measure at
40k-80k tokens"*. The parent item is that revisit, so the harness must be
trustworthy at that size first. Today `build_prompt()` targets ~4 chars/token
without reporting llama-server's real `prompt_tokens`, `--sizes` is free-form,
and a single 80k prefill can take minutes under GPU contention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The harness records llama-server's reported `prompt_tokens` per sample
  and fails loudly when the delivered size deviates from the requested size by
  more than 10 %, so a mis-sized prompt cannot silently invalidate a bin.
- AC2: An end-to-end run at `--sizes 40960,61440,81920 --reps 3` produces a
  JSON result with per-size p50/p90 and the 20k+ headline aggregate within a
  documented time budget and timeout.
- AC3: Offline unit tests cover prompt sizing/token accounting, percentile
  aggregation, size-deviation rejection and argument validation - no live
  server required.
- AC4: `docs/dev/` records the band methodology and validity guards: unique
  prompt text per repetition, `cache_prompt: false`, the TTS/GPU-contention
  noise rule, and minimum reps.
- AC5: Full suite green via the test skill.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` - the A/B harness
- `tests/test_ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` - offline harness tests
- `docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md` - prior experiment record to extend

## Implementation sketch (test-first)

1. Extend the offline tests for the new validations.
2. Report and validate actual `prompt_tokens`; fail fast on a mis-sized bin.
3. Add a documented default band (`40960,61440,81920`) and a per-size timeout
   policy.
4. Record the methodology in `docs/dev/`.

## Dependencies

- Verify sustained local utilisation gate.
- Experiment: 1 slot at 262K ctx vs 2 slots at 131K ctx (LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN) -
  a 40-80k prompt must fit the per-slot context.

## Out of scope

Changing llama-server flags, routing or admission policy.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want `--ubatch-size` and `--batch-size` re-measured in the
40-80k band against a pre-registered win threshold, so the values shipped in
`models.ini` are justified by measurement rather than inherited.

## Context

- Current `[Qwen3]` launch flags: `--ctx-size 262144 --parallel 2
  --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 1024 --cache-ram 40960 --cache-type-k q8_0
  --cache-type-v q8_0 --swa-checkpoints 32 --no-mmap -ngl 80 --threads 8`,
  plus `flash-attn`.
- Prior A/B (LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS, `docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md`): 1.04x
  at p90 over 20k+ batches, reverted. Its close-out rule is that a retry must
  be measured at 40-80k.
- Geometry interacts: per-slot context (`--ctx-size / --parallel`) bounds the
  largest prompt the harness can send, so this item starts only after the
  geometry experiment has recorded its decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC2: Prefill throughput is improved by tuning the llama-server launch configuration, each changed value justified by measurement rather than guesswork, or reverted and recorded.
- AC1: A hypothesis and numeric decision gate are written on this item BEFORE
  the first measurement (for example: adopt when p90 prompt-eval tok/s improves
  by >= 1.3x in the 60-80k bins with decode regression <= 2 %).
- AC2: Candidate values (`--ubatch-size` 2048 and 4096; `--batch-size` 8192 vs
  16384) are measured one variable at a time on arm-identical workloads with
  >= 3 reps using the 40-80k band harness; raw JSON is archived under
  `benchmark-results/`.
- AC3: Each knob gets an explicit adopt/revert decision with measured numbers;
  an adopted value is written to `models.ini` `[Qwen3]` with the measurement
  and rollback value in the comment, a rejected value is recorded as reverted
  to 1024 / 8192.
- AC4: VRAM and stability are checked per arm (clean llama-server start, no
  OOM, `rocm-smi` within budget); the restart that empties the 40 GiB prompt
  cache is recorded so proxy first-byte stats are not compared across it.
- AC5: Any test or script asserting the flags is updated in the same change and
  the full suite is green via the test skill.
- AC6: If no value wins, the item completes with a recorded NO-GO and the
  parent's tuning scope narrows to the proxy-knob/ETA-guard half.

**Key Files:**
- `./models.ini` - `[Qwen3]` launch flags
- `./start-llama.sh` - flag defaults passed to llama-server
- `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` - measurement harness
- `tests/test_models_ini_centralized_config.sh` - flag assertions
- `docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md` - prior record to extend
- `benchmark-results/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22-candidate-2048.json` - prior raw arm data

## Dependencies

- Verify sustained local utilisation gate.
- Baseline prefill measurement capture.
- 40-80k prefill benchmark capability.
- Experiment: 1 slot at 262K ctx vs 2 slots at 131K ctx (LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN).

## Out of scope

`--cache-ram`, KV-cache quantisation, ctx-size/slot geometry, `--threads`,
`--mlock` and `--swa-checkpoints` (see the sibling launch-flag item).

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the prefill-ETA admission guard and the prefill
deadline re-checked against the post-change prefill rates and the interaction
documented, so a faster GPU cannot silently make the budget/deadline wrong.

## Context

- Live knobs - deployed by LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D, do **not** re-tune without new
  evidence: `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens: 25000`,
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 120`,
  `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens: 20000`,
  `local_admission_guard_budget_safety_fraction: 0.95`,
  `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile: 75`,
  `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds: 600`.
- The guard calibrates itself from a rolling window of per-dispatch samples
  `(coded_tokens, new_tokens, dispatch_to_first_byte_ms)` keyed by
  `(model, context bucket)`, so it re-calibrates automatically. But the budget
  (25k) and deadline (120 s) were derived from the OLD band rates (249 t/s at
  20-30k, 114 t/s at 63k). If prefill becomes materially faster, both may be
  re-derivable - a decision for measurement, not guesswork.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC2: Prefill throughput is improved by tuning the configuration (llama-server launch flags and the prefill-related proxy knobs) where measurement justifies each change, otherwise left unchanged and recorded.
- AC4: If a knob change affects the prefill-ETA guard's behaviour, the guard's configuration and documentation are updated together, and the local_prefill_deadline_seconds / ETA interactions are documented.
- AC1: Matched before/after windows compare guard behaviour: admit vs reject
  counts by reason (`prefill_budget_exceeded`, `eta_exceeds_budget`,
  `prefill_deadline_exceeded`), thrash-cooldown events and cancelled prefills.
- AC2: The measured band rates (10-20k, 20-30k, 30-40k, 40-60k, 60-80k) are
  re-derived from the post-change window and compared numerically with the
  rates the budget and deadline were derived from.
- AC3: A decision is recorded on whether 25 000 tokens / 120 s remain optimal;
  any change is justified by AC1/AC2 numbers, shipped in one change with its
  config comment, and carries a documented rollback.
- AC4: The `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` <-> ETA-guard <->
  contention-queue interaction (the ordering invariant
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds < local_prefill_deadline_seconds <
  local_dispatch_first_byte_timeout_seconds < local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`)
  is documented in one authoritative place (config comments plus a `docs/dev/`
  note) and the tests asserting the ordering still pass.
- AC5: Guard/calibration code is unchanged unless a measured defect is found;
  if changed, unit tests cover the new behaviour.
- AC6: Full suite green via the test skill.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` - calibration and admission guard
- `proxy/config.yaml` - guard, budget and deadline configuration
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta.py` - calibration tests
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py` - conservative pricing tests
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_deadline.py` - deadline interaction tests

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want Arm B (1 slot at 262,144 ctx) measured over a window of
identical length to Arm A, with the slot-count and context-dependent settings
adjusted consistently, so the geometry trade-off is measurable without a
threshold confound.

## Context

- Per-slot ctx is `--ctx-size / --parallel`: `--parallel 1 --ctx-size 262144` -> 262,144 per slot. `--parallel` and `session_slot_pool_size` MUST match or sessions map to nonexistent slots.
- The warm ceiling is `min(clamp, economic)` with economic = `round(local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio x local_model_ctx_size)` (0.4578 x 262,144 ~= 120,049) and clamp = 258,048 at 1 slot. Leaving the ratio unchanged keeps the warm cap at ~120K, so the extra slot context would never be routed to - the ratio/threshold must be raised so the ceiling matches the new clamp (parent AC2: "adjusted consistently").
- The cold/warm band must keep non-zero width or the cached_ratio routing check stays unreachable (LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 / LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP).
- `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` becomes moot with one slot (prefill serialisation is inherent); record whether it is left as-is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Geometry changes are applied together and verified after restart: llama-server reports 1 slot with n_ctx 262,144, `session_slot_pool_size: 1`, warm ceiling raised to the 258,048 clamp (or an explicit recorded justification for keeping ~120K), cold threshold unchanged at 38,000. Band width and cached_ratio-check reachability are demonstrated from the routing code / unit tests, not assumed.
- AC2: Arm B is measured over a window of the same length as Arm A inside a >= 60 % busy night; raw data archived under `benchmark-results/`; reporter output recorded on this item and on the parent.
- AC3: A rollback is recorded (exact values and command to restore Arm A) and the cache-emptying restart is marked so first-byte stats are not compared across it.
- AC4: Any serving errors introduced (slot_save failed, HTTP 400/503, slot-mismatch warnings) are captured in the arm's metric table.

- Parent AC2 trace: Arm A (2 x 131K, current) and Arm B (1 x 262K) are each run for a comparable period at the gate, with llama-server --parallel / --ctx-size changed together and session_slot_pool_size plus the warm/cold thresholds adjusted consistently.

data.description:
## Problem

`proxy/proxy/handlers.py:489` carries a `# noqa` comment whose text is prose
rather than a comma-separated code list, so ruff cannot parse it as a
suppression. Every `ruff check` run in this repo — repo-wide or file-scoped —
prints a warning to stderr:

```
$ ruff check --select I001 proxy/proxy/handlers.py
warning: Invalid `# noqa` directive on proxy/proxy/handlers.py:489: expected a
comma-separated list of codes (e.g. `# noqa: F401, F841`).
All checks passed!
```

Current source:

```python
    import os  # noqa: local import for config access
```

## Why it matters

- The comment gives no suppression at all: whatever it was intended to silence
  (`F401`? a local-import / `PLC0415` style rule?) is either already allowed by
  `.ruff.toml` or silently expressed as prose — so the intent is unrecoverable
  from the code.
- It makes every lint invocation in this repository noisy, which trains readers
  and agents to ignore ruff's warning channel — the exact channel that would
  surface a genuinely broken suppression.
- It was noted as a known-but-out-of-scope side observation while clearing the
  `I001` findings of epic `LP-0MVLK5H04003FZJS` (see
  `LP-0MVKE61H9001WPAQ` for the earlier sighting).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — warning cleared:** `python3 -m ruff check proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
      produces no `Invalid \`noqa\` directive` warning and still reports
      `All checks passed!` (command + output captured on the work item).
- [ ] **AC2 — intent preserved:** the reason for the directive is expressed
      either as a valid code list (e.g. `# noqa: PLC0415`) that matches the
      rule actually triggered, or as a plain explanatory comment with no
      `noqa` prefix. Determined by removing the directive and re-running ruff
      on the file to see which rule (if any) fires; recorded in the closure
      comment.
- [ ] **AC3 — no blanket suppression:** `.ruff.toml` gains no new
      `per-file-ignores`/global `ignore` entry for `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`,
      so genuine future findings remain detectable (`git diff --stat` on
      `.ruff.toml` empty for this item).
- [ ] **AC4 — no behaviour change:** the change is comment-only; the
      `import os` statement itself is untouched, so runtime behaviour is
      identical.
- [ ] **AC5 — full suite green:** validation runs through the test skill
      (`/skill:test`, changed scope at the implement gate, full suite at the
      dev-push gate) — no ad-hoc `pytest`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — line 489 holds the invalid directive
  (`import os  # noqa: local import for config access`).
- `.ruff.toml` — **must remain unchanged**; no suppression may be added.

## Provenance

Discovered from: `LP-0MVLK5H04003FZJS` (Quality Improvement - Refactoring epic) while
closing child `LP-0MVMLII27004JVII` — that item verified
`ruff check --select I001 .` clean at HEAD `9db15857` and this stray `# noqa`
warning was the only remaining lint-channel noise observed. Earlier sighting
recorded in `LP-0MVKE61H9001WPAQ`. Not blocking that epic: the epic tracks
`I001` findings, and this is a distinct (pre-existing) hygiene defect.

data.description:
## Goal

Track the parent AC4 residual found by the post-deploy measurement (LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I): within-budget warm prompts that are admitted, then cancelled by the 120 s prefill deadline with **zero prefill progress** — second-slot head-of-line blocking, not the admission budget.

> **Plan note (2026-10-28) — hypothesis superseded.** The scheduler epic LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG and LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE are completed, yet the residual survived; a later window (LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27) shows 68 % of these evictions overlap no other prefill, so the cause is predicted-not-measured warmth, not second-slot head-of-line blocking. The live fix owner is LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (with F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD). The *Ownership* and *Key Files* sections below are stale on this point; the AC text is unchanged and the closure verdict is owned by child LP-0MVRMOV8K0007NFO.

## Evidence (2026-10-25 11:46:50 → 19:11, post-deploy window of LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D)

- 22 `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=prefill_deadline` events over 7.4 h (2.97/h vs the 24.3/h baseline → −88 %), all with `new_tokens ≤ 25 000` (so all within the shipped budget) and ETA ≤ 68 s for the small ones (e.g. `eta_prefill_s=7.1 elapsed_s=120.1`, `eta_prefill_s=20.4 elapsed_s=120.1`, `eta_prefill_s=24.8 elapsed_s=120.2`).
- The common signature is `lease_extended_during_prefill … progress=None alive=False in_flight=True` repeated for the whole lease plus `prefill_wait_exceeds_threshold waited=30s progress=0` — the llama task makes **no progress at all** for 120 s while the other slot serves a prefill. E.g. a 13.3k-token cold prompt sat behind an audit session's huge prefill for the full lease.
- 10 of the 22 events are sibling-epic audit loads (`audit-LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG-*`, `audit-AH-*`, drive session `01a172f6…`); user-traffic residual = 12 events / 7.4 h = 1.6/h.
- Every over-budget (>25 k new-token) prompt was refused at admission in the window (zero over-budget admissions, `prefill_budget_exceeded` refusals 1 089) — the budget half of the parent is working; only the *warm, small-ETA* residual survives, and it is a scheduler/occupancy problem.

## Ownership

The scheduler epic **LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG** (session-level tenancy / resident-prefix admission, serialised prefills LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ) covers exactly this class: per-request scheduling against the 2-slot pool with no occupancy-aware admission. This item is a **tracking/evidence item** for the parent's AC4; it is deliberately not implemented here (out of this parent's scope).

## Scope

**In:** evidence, link to the scheduler epic, closure criteria, and the parent-AC4 re-scope note. The eventual fix (occupancy-aware admission: refuse a local dispatch when the other slot is mid-prefill and the projected total exceeds the deadline) is scheduled on LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG.

**Out:** changes to this parent's budget/deadline maths; any work already owned by the scheduler epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Evidence recorded.** The 22-event/7.4 h measurement (12 user-traffic) with the `progress=0` signature and the audit-load split is referenced from the parent AC4 comment.
- **AC2 — Link established.** A related edge points to LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG so the producer can fold this into the scheduler scope (or explicitly re-scope parent AC4 to exclude audit traffic / warm-HOL).
- **AC3 — Closure.** Closed only when either (a) the scheduler epic lands and a post-landing window shows zero user-traffic `prefill_deadline` evictions after acceptance, or (b) the producer explicitly re-scopes parent AC4 with an agreed threshold and the re-scoped criterion is met.
- **AC4 — Rollback note.** No rollback recommended: the budget change is working (−88 % deadline rate, 0 over-budget admissions, −83 % wasted tokens); rolling back restores the thrash without touching this residual.

## Key Files

- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` (window evidence)
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (occupancy-aware `ProjectedWait` exists; the scheduler epic consumes it)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` (`_try_acquire_local_dispatch` prefill gate)
## Relationships

- **discovered-from: LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D** (cold-prefill admission budget epic) — found by its post-deploy measurement (LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I).
- **depends-on: LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG** (local slot scheduling epic) — the fix is occupancy-aware admission / prefill scheduling, owned there.
- **Detached from LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D's children (2026-10-25).** It was filed as a child of that epic, but it depends on the scheduler epic's multi-day horizon, and a parent cannot advance to `in_review` while any child is still open — keeping it as a child would have made the admission-budget epic unable to close after its own 24 h window. It is therefore a standalone tracking item: the budget epic closes on its re-scoped AC4; this item closes on its own AC3.
## Implementation and measurement vehicles (added at intake, 2026-10-25)

The fix and the closing measurement are separate items; this item owns only the evidence, the link and the closure verdict.

- **`LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE` — `[impl] Occupancy-aware deadline admission (second-slot head-of-line residual)`** (child of the scheduler epic `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`, `intake_complete`, implementation started 2026-10-25T23:08Z). It prices the projected time-to-first-byte from the **occupant's** own admission evidence (`eta_prefill_s` − elapsed) and refuses with `reason=prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline` when the projection exceeds `local_prefill_deadline_seconds`. Its "Out of scope" section names this item's AC3 as the owner of the ≥24 h post-landing measurement — i.e. the fix lands there, the verdict is recorded here.
- **`LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I` — `Post-deploy 24 h prefill regression verification`** (top level, implementable from `2026-10-26 20:17:00 UTC`) reports the post-acceptance eviction counter and its per-reason breakdown for the **budget** window. It is a different window and a different baseline from this item's closure window (which starts when the occupancy-aware admission lands), so its verdict must not be reused as AC3 evidence.

### AC3 closure conditions, made concrete

- **(a)** `LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE` lands, and a ≥24 h window starting **after** its deploy shows **zero user-traffic** `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=prefill_deadline` events (audit sessions reported separately, as in the parent AC4 re-scope). A residual that is shown to be GPU incapacity rather than occupancy — measured, with the same evidence standard as the 22-event baseline — also satisfies (a).
- **(b)** The producer explicitly re-scopes parent AC4 with an agreed threshold and that re-scoped criterion is met.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — the residual is occupancy, not capacity.** The `progress=None alive=False in_flight=True` signature (no prefill progress for the whole lease while the other slot serves) is the diagnostic; the occupant-evidence pricing in `LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE` is the matching fix. If the post-landing window still shows zero-progress evictions, the measurement must separate occupant starvation from GPU saturation before AC3 can be closed.
- **Risk — window contamination.** A restart, config reload or slot-count change inside the closure window re-bases it; record the deploy timestamp of `LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE` on this item before the window opens.
- **Risk — attribution.** 10 of the 22 baseline events were sibling-epic audit loads; the user-traffic / audit split must use the same classifier as the parent AC4 measurement so the two reports stay comparable.
- **Scope-creep risk — further admission-maths tuning.** Any additional change to budgets, deadlines, queue bounds or slot counts discovered while measuring is filed as a linked work item on `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`, not folded into this tracking item.

## Intake notes (auto-complete)

- **Evaluation:** intake interview not required — the item already carries a measured evidence window, four testable acceptance criteria, key files, dependency edges and a producer-decided scope. Advanced via `intake.py auto-complete` (no clarifying questions asked; no Appendix required because no interview took place).
- **Duplicate check (2026-10-25):** searched `prefill_deadline`, `head-of-line`, `occupancy-aware`, `resident-prefix` and `prefill deadline`. No completed or open item fully satisfies this item's ACs: `LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE` implements the fix and explicitly out-scopes the measurement here; `LP-0MVO7IDTP005S92D` (completed) excluded the 22 genuine `prefill_deadline` events from its scope; `LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5` evaluates the snapshot-pool size. Partial overlap only — no rewrite required.
- **Issue type corrected** `feature` → `task`: the deliverable is evidence, a link and a closure verdict, not new capability (the capability is `LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE`).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

# Intake Brief — Lease fairness: cap consecutive prefill-lease renewals so one session cannot monopolise the local gate

## Problem statement

One session can hold the local gate for many minutes by chaining
`lease_extended_during_prefill` renewals (with or without a first byte), while
concurrent sessions queue up to the contention budget (60–120 s) and fall back
to paid remote providers. Observed 2026-10-23: session `herdr-1792789684-1790656-13656`
held the local lease ~19 min with continuous renewal while three other sessions
queued 60 s and fell back (`contention_queue_fallback_after_queue
reason=local_lease_active`). The lease must be fairly shared: a bounded hold per
session while others are queued, without regressing warm-slot affinity for
successful turns.

## Users

- **Operator** (primary) — wants the local gate shared fairly across sessions so
  no single session monopolises capacity while others pay remote fallback costs.
  - *User story*: "As an operator, I want a session that has held the local gate
    for an unbounded chain of `progress=None` renewals to be cut off near the
    prefill deadline, so queued sessions get served instead of falling back."
  - *User story*: "As an operator, I want a session that already delivered a
    first byte but keeps renewing across turn boundaries to give queued sessions
    a bounded window, while still keeping its warm slot priority."
- **Concurrent sessions** (secondary) — experience queue-then-fallback latency and
  cost when a monopoliser holds the gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. [impl] A bounded hold bound exists for `lease_extended_during_prefill ...
   progress=None` chains: total prefill-hold without a first byte is capped
   near `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (e.g. deadline + overhead), with a
   regression test. The bound applies regardless of extension signal
   (including `in_flight=True`), and releases the gate so a queued session is
   admitted.
2. A session that has already delivered a first byte may not extend its lease
   indefinitely while other sessions queue: a bounded-max hold (or yielding)
   with a regression test — **mechanism pending producer decision (Appendix Q1)**
   — release at request boundary / between-turn yield is the recommended shape;
   no mid-stream kill of a producing stream (Appendix Q2).
3. Warm-slot affinity for successful turns is preserved: a session that recently
   completed a local turn still re-acquires the same slot/warm KV (no regression
   against `prefill_extended_streams` behaviour). With the recommended
   between-turn yield this is preserved via the contention-queue retention
   mechanism (`contention_queue.retained` waiters ahead of newcomers).
4. The 24 h post-fix window measurement re-run after the change shows the
   productive-holder denial class materially reduced (target: -50 % vs the
   classification baseline) while `ac1.wedge_denials` stays 0. Re-run via
   `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py --measure`; baseline/window
   confirmed in Appendix Q3.
5. [test] Validation: hermetic regression tests plus the full project test suite
   pass with the new changes (continuous-renewal monopoliser bounded; first-byte
   session bounded without mid-stream truncation; warm-slot affinity preserved;
   `0`-valued knobs restore pre-change behaviour).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes —
   `proxy/config.yaml` knob comments, `proxy/README.md` / `proxy/docs/routing.md`
   lease section, and `docs/dev/prefill-recovery-verification.md` for the AC4
   re-run procedure and results.

## Constraints

- **No mid-stream kill of a producing stream** (recommended; pending Q2): a
  stream that has delivered a first byte and is actively generating occupies a
  physical slot in a single-slot pool — pre-empting it would truncate the
  holder's turn and would not free the slot for real work anyway.
- **Warm-slot affinity is intentional** (epic assumption, LP-0MVLHMCN6003GAMD):
  lease retention for explicit sessions with cache history must survive the
  fairness change.
- Extension signals that are **not** progress must not count as progress: an
  open in-flight request already does not refresh `last_progress_ts`
  (LP-0MVKUKFSO008GI6O AC4); the fairness cap must not reintroduce a wedge-shape
  that defeats the 180 s no-progress watchdog.
- The wedge defect shape is tracked separately (LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV, in-request
  re-dispatch after prefill-deadline cancellation re-arming the lease); the
  fairness cap here must not mask or duplicate that defect.
- Config-consistent: any new knob is documented in `proxy/config.yaml` (and the
  cheap/fast profiles if changes are needed) with a rollback default.

## Existing state

- `_extend_lease_during_prefill` (router_helpers.py) pushes `expires_at` out by
  `local_dispatch_lease_prefill_buffer_seconds` (30 s) on numeric progress
  advance, observed slot liveness, or the caller's own in-flight marker —
  every 10 s poll. There is **no per-session hold counter** and no
  cap on consecutive `progress=None` renewals.
- `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 120` cancels a no-first-byte dispatch in the
  router and releases the lease (`lease_released reason=prefill_deadline`); its
  `_watchdog_no_progress` bound is 180 s. These are per-request backstops and do
  not bound a session's *chain* of renewals across requests/turns.
- 24 h post-fix window (LP-0MVM83F6X0005V8S, commit 458c7fc6):
  `local_dispatch_denied` = 306 short-hold / 141 stale-owner / 2
  productive-holder / 0 wedge; max productive hold 190 s, max unproductive
  164 s; `prefill_extended_streams` = 1975.
- Later window (2026-10-26, comment LP-C0MVPUC5E2003ZVF5): 3 wedge-attributed
  denials separated out to LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV (blocking-edge input).

## Desired change

- **AC1 (recommended, no open decision):** track per-dispatch
  no-first-byte hold start; refuse extension (all signals) once
  `now − first_acquisition >= bound`, where bound defaults to
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds + buffer` (150 s at defaults) behind a new
  config knob `local_dispatch_no_first_byte_hold_seconds`. Release the gate at
  the bound so a queued session is admitted; regression test.
- **AC2 (mechanism pending producer decision, Appendix Q1/Q2):** recommended
  shape is a request-boundary yield — cap same-session re-acquisition while the
  contention queue holds other-session waiters (with retention priority
  preserving warm-slot affinity), rather than a mid-stream kill. Alternative
  considered: hard-abort the holder's stream at the bound (rejected: destructive,
  oversubscribes the physical slot).
- **AC4:** re-run `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py --measure` on the 24 h
  window after deploy; gate on productive-holder denials −50 % vs the
  2/306/141 baseline with `ac1.wedge_denials == 0`.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_extend_lease_during_prefill` (~line 1491),
  `_get_prefill_lease_config` (~line 1015), `mark_local_first_byte`,
  `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (~line 2679), `_dispatch_lease_key` (~line 50):
  hold tracking, extension cap, re-acquisition gating.
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py` — queued-waiter visibility for the
  yield/deny decision (`retained` waiters, `contention_queue_retention`).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `local_lease_active` deny/fallback paths
  (~lines 6890–11490).
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `local_prefill_*` section (deadline 120 s, thrash
  cooldown 600 s), new fairness knobs.
- `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py` — `ac1` attribution for AC4
  (`productive_holder_denials`, `wedge_denials`).
- Tests: `proxy/tests/test_prefill_lease_extension.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_lease_truthfulness.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_retention.py`.

## Related work

- LP-0MVLHMCN6003GAMD (completed, in_review) — "Post-fix local gate still
  denies queued sessions"; its 2026-10-25 producer decision on AC1 (option A
  restated the wedge AC) routed option B's fairness work to this item. No open
  dependency edge (that item is terminal); recorded as provenance only.
- LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV (open, intake_complete) — in-request local re-dispatch
  after deadline cancellation re-arms the lease (the wedge narrow defect);
  fairness cap alone does not fix that re-dispatch — linked, not duplicated.
- LP-0MVKUKFSO008GI6O (completed) — in-flight signal no longer refreshes
  `last_progress_ts`; `proxy/tests/test_lease_truthfulness.py` pins the
  contract the fairness cap must preserve.
- LP-0MVKUKFHH005UDWL (completed) — post-deadline prefill-thrash cooldown
  (per-session), the per-session precedent for fairness knobs.
- LP-0MVK35HBI003SB3Z (open) — lease-gate shape attribution in idle-admit
  measurement (feeds AC4 classification).
- Docs: `docs/dev/in-flight-lease-hold-characterisation.md` (superseded),
  `docs/dev/contention-queue-lease-retention.md`,
  `docs/dev/prefill-recovery-verification.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** the in-request re-dispatch wedge (LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV) is a
  separate defect; verify the fairness change does not paper over it. New
  observation opportunities (e.g. per-hold-content time series) go to new work
  items, not this one.
- **False kill of a legitimate long prefill:** the no-first-byte cap must sit at
  or above the deadline so it cannot fire before the deadline's own cancellation;
  genuine long prefills (>180 s observed) still need the in-flight/liveness
  extension, so the cap targets *chains spanning multiple requests*, not one
  long prefill.
- **Warm-slot regression from AC2:** the between-turn yield must route the
  holder's next request back to the same slot/warm KV via retention; a naive
  lease-drop between turns would evict KV and reintroduce re-prefill thrash.
- **AC4 measurement variance:** 24 h windows are noisy; the −50 % target is
  directional, and `ac1.wedge_denials == 0` is the hard gate.
- **Interaction with the thrash cooldown (600 s):** a refused extension plus the
  per-session `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds` could compound into a long
  local skip for the affected session; the cap must not stack multiplicatively
  with the cooldown into a self-inflicted local outage.
- **Assumption:** defaults for new knobs preserve current behaviour except the
  bounded hold, so a misconfig is rollback-safe (`0` disables a knob).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which mechanism should AC2 use to bound a first-byte session's hold while
  others queue?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — recommended: (a)
  request-boundary yield — cap same-session re-acquisition while the contention
  queue holds other sessions, holder re-queues with retention priority; vs (b)
  hard max session hold that aborts the next extension; vs (c) per-request lease
  cycle only (extensions never outlive the request). Research: single-slot pool
  physically cannot share a slot mid-generation; observed max productive hold
  190 s < 300 s wedge bound; `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` allows same-session
  re-acquisition unconditionally, which is the AC2 gap.
- Q2: "May the fairness bound ever pre-empt (kill) a stream that has already
  delivered a first byte and is still producing?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION
  (producer)** — recommended: No — never kill a producing stream for fairness;
  AC2's bound applies at request boundaries / extension refusal, not mid-stream.
  Evidence: a 19-min monopoliser *did* serve local streams; killing truncates
  the holder's turn and frees no physical slot.
- Q3: "What is the baseline and verification window for AC4's −50 % target?"
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — recommended: reuse the
  LP-0MVM83F6X0005V8S 24 h post-fix classification baseline
  (2 productive-holder / 306 short-hold / 141 stale-owner) and the same
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py --measure` window shape (24 h
  post-deploy), with the implementer/operator confirming the window start.
  Research: description baseline is the 2026-10-23 post-fix window; the
  2026-10-25 window added 3 wedge denials attributed to LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV,
  which the AC re-run must exclude.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MR9G183O004SJLO** – Add local_owner_session_id to /llama/local/status endpoint (completed)
- **LP-0MSJ7W7YE003HETO** – Hermetic tests: prefill-progress lease extension (completed)
- **LP-0MV0MM5R60025XZE** – Cap exhaustion retry timer at 60 minutes for clients (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: abort, aborts, ac1, ac2, ac4 (+326 more)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0mvkukfhh005udwl, 0mvkukfso008gi6o, abort, aborts, ac1 (+319 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: abort, ac1, ac2, ac4, acceptance (+316 more)

## Summary

Measure whether the child-port discovery fix (LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF, deployed
2026-10-26T21:01Z) actually eliminates router-responder `GET /slots ... 500`
responses over a full 24 h production window, and record the raw counts as
auditable evidence.

**Earliest run: 2026-10-27T12:00Z.** Window:
**2026-10-27T12:00Z → 2026-10-28T12:00Z.** If the fix (or a follow-up restart)
lands later than that, shift the window to start 24 h after the last relevant
deployment and record the new timestamps in a comment.

**Window state verified at planning (2026-10-28T04:40Z):** the window is
**still open** (≈7 h 20 m remaining at verification time). Production facts:
proxy pid **3791954** started **2026-10-27T10:16:11Z** and is still running
(18 h 23 m uptime) — the fixed proxy has been up continuously since **before**
the window opened, and **no proxy restart has occurred inside the window**, so
the AC6 restart condition is satisfiable. No pre-window baseline comment was
recorded at 12:00Z; see "Baseline reconstruction" under the execute-time plan
for why the counter delta is nonetheless provable.

## Problem statement

Router-proxied `GET /slots` polls returned HTTP 500 at ~9 % during giant
prefills because child-port discovery silently failed and every proxy poll
traversed the router. The fix replaced discovery with a rotation-proof signal
and routed every call site through it, but the only proof that matters is a
production 24 h window with zero such 500s — the pre-fix evidence (1,754
router 500s in the 2026-10-26 log) is not proof of absence.

## Users

- **Producer / maintainer** — "As the operator, I want a dated, reproducible
  measurement of router-responder `/slots` 500s so I can close the residual-500
  bug and trust the fix, instead of re-reading raw logs myself."
- **On-call agent (herdr downtime worker)** — "As an unattended agent, I want a
  deterministic method and explicit verdict rule so my pass/fail report does
  not depend on my own judgement of ambiguous counts."
- **Downstream users** — chat/agent clients that see 500s and 5–7 s slot-poll
  latency when slot queries serialise behind a busy child.

## Acceptance Criteria

Refined at intake per producer decisions Q1(a), Q2(b), Q3(a):

- **AC1** — **Chat-model path: zero.** The windowed count of router-responder
  `GET /slots ... 500` responses attributable to the chat model is **0**.
  Responder split: lines with no `[pid]` prefix are the router, `[pid]`-prefixed
  lines are the model children; per-file counts are reported for every
  `llama-server*.log` file whose mtime falls inside the window (Q1a).
- **AC2** — **Raw router and child counts reported**, so a silent switch back to
  router polling cannot masquerade as a pass: router-responder `GET /slots`
  200 / 400 / 500 and model-child 200 / 400 / 500 counts for each file in the
  window. `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` output is attached verbatim.
- **AC3** — **`slots_stale` share reported** for `status_request` polls in the
  window: the primary figure is *all* `status_request` polls (directly
  comparable to the pre-fix baseline **579/899** in the 2026-10-26 file), with
  the active-prefill subset (`active_query=true` or `local_active_query=true`)
  reported as a secondary figure (Q3a).
- **AC4** — **Fallback evidence reported, split by path** (Q2b):
  `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  delta across the window plus the (throttled, undercounting)
  `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning lines, attributed by model.
  - Chat-model (`Qwen3`) fallbacks: **any occurrence fails the check.**
  - Embed-model (`mxbai-embed`) fallbacks: reported separately as a
    **non-blocking observation**; if any occur, a new bug item is filed at
    window end, linked `discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`.
- **AC5** — **Reproducibility:** the exact commands/regexes (or script
  invocations) used, the window start/end timestamps, the pre-window baseline
  snapshot (counter values, log line count, proxy pid + start time) and the raw
  counts are all recorded as a work-item comment.
- **AC6** — **Restart integrity:** any proxy restart inside the window is
  detected (pid change) and reported; if one occurred, the counter delta is
  declared unavailable and the verdict relies on per-file log counts with the
  limitation stated explicitly.
- **AC7** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC8** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Method (agreed: Q1 option (a) — hybrid)

Measured with existing tooling plus two log families:

```bash
# 1. Window-start snapshot (also record: date -u, pid start time, log line count)
date -u; ps -o lstart= -p "$(pgrep -f 'uvicorn proxy.server:app')"
wc -l < /var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log
curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep 'llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total'

# 2. Window-end snapshot (same commands, 24 h later) -> counter delta = exact
#    windowed fallbacks when the proxy was not restarted in between.

# 3. Responder/status split per file (reuses the triage CLI: no timestamps in
#    llama-server logs, so scope by the files whose mtime falls in the window)
python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --llama-file 'llama-server.log' --summary

# 4. Fallback warnings (throttled to one line per interval -> undercounts;
#    the counter above is authoritative)
grep -c 'slots_child_port_unavailable' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log

# slots_stale share (existing baseline method)
grep -o 'slots_stale=[a-z]*' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log | sort | uniq -c
```

Take a **pre-window baseline snapshot** immediately before
2026-10-27T12:00Z (counter values + `llama-server.log` line count + proxy pid
start time) so the window delta is unambiguous.

> **Status: not done.** No snapshot comment exists for 2026-10-27T12:00Z. The
execution plan below reconstructs the baseline from monotonic-counter
evolution plus pid `lstart`, and states the limitation explicitly (AC5).

## Execution plan (exact recipe — run at/after 2026-10-28T12:00Z)

Steps 0–2 must be re-verified at run time, not trusted from this block; they
are read-only and cheap. Steps 3–6 produce the evidence; step 7 records it.

### Step 0 — window gate

Do **not** measure before **2026-10-28T12:00Z**. An earlier run measures a
partial window and is not acceptable as the AC evidence.

### Step 1 — restart integrity (AC6)

```bash
date -u
ps -o pid,lstart,etime -p "$(pgrep -f 'uvicorn proxy.server:app' | head -1)"
```

Expected: a single pid **3791954** with `lstart` **2026-10-27T10:16:11Z** ⇒ no
restart inside the window. Any other pid/`lstart` ⇒ record the restart time,
declare the counter delta unavailable, and fall back to per-file log counts
with the limitation stated (AC6).

### Step 2 — fallback counter (AC4, exact)

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep 'llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total'
```

A Prometheus counter that has never been incremented emits **no sample line**
(only `# HELP` / `# TYPE`). That is the state observed at planning — quote the
raw output verbatim, because "absent sample" is the auditable form of "0".
Range-vector deltas are not needed: a monotonic counter reading 0 on a process
that started before the window ⇒ windowed delta = 0.

### Baseline reconstruction (AC5, replaces the missed 12:00Z snapshot)

State the limitation explicitly and rebuild the baseline from: proxy pid +
`lstart` (step 1); the counter's never-incremented state (step 2); the per-file
line counts read at window end. The proof is monotonicity, not a start sample:
the process started 1 h 44 m before the window opened and its counter is still
0.

### Step 3 — llama-server file set (AC1 / AC2)

```bash
ls -l --time-style=full-iso /var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server*.log*
```

Window set (mtime inside 2026-10-27T12:00Z → 2026-10-28T12:00Z):
`llama-server.log-2026-10-28` (logrotate `copytruncate` copy at 00:00Z; content
= 2026-10-27T00:00Z → 2026-10-28T00:00Z) and the live `llama-server.log`
(content = 2026-10-28T00:00Z → window end). `llama-server.log-2026-10-27.gz`
has mtime 2026-10-27T00:00Z ⇒ outside the window, exclude it.

llama-server access lines carry **no timestamps**, so this union covers
2026-10-27T00:00Z → window end: a **superset** of the window, carrying 12 h of
extra pre-window traffic. Consequence: **zero router-responder 500s across the
superset proves zero inside the window** (report the over-count direction); a
non-zero count needs the per-file split plus the caveat that the window
boundary is approximate at ±12 h granularity.

```bash
python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
  --llama-file 'llama-server.log-2026-10-28' --summary
python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
  --llama-file 'llama-server.log' --summary
```

Record both per-file outputs verbatim (AC2) and sum the responder/status matrix
(router 200/400/500, child 200/400/500).

### Step 4 — proxy.log file set (AC3, plus AC4 warnings)

`proxy.log` is timestamped and self-rotates every 6 h, and the daily
`copytruncate` copy (`proxy.log-YYYY-MM-DD_HH`) can duplicate a range — so
**file names do not reliably delimit the window**. Derive each candidate's own
first/last timestamp from its lines, keep the parts intersecting the window,
and dedupe overlapping ranges (keep one generation per timestamp range):

```bash
for f in /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*; do
  case "$f" in *.gz) zcat "$f";; *) cat "$f";; esac \
    | awk -v f="$f" 'NR==1{first=$0} {last=$0} END{print f"	"substr(first,1,19)"	"substr(last,1,19)}'
done
```

At planning time the window-relevant generations were
`proxy.log.2026-10-27_10`, `proxy.log.2026-10-27_16`, `proxy.log.2026-10-27_22`,
`proxy.log-2026-10-28_00` and the live `proxy.log` — indicative only; re-derive
the set from timestamps at run time.

```bash
# AC3 primary: all status_request polls in the window (comparable to 579/899)
grep -h 'status_request' <window files> | grep -o 'slots_stale=[a-z]*' | sort | uniq -c
# AC3 secondary: active-prefill subset
grep -h 'status_request' <window files> \
  | grep -o 'active_query=[a-z]*\|local_active_query=[a-z]*' | sort | uniq -c
# AC4 warnings, per file (throttled -> undercounts; the step-2 counter is authoritative)
for f in <window files>; do printf '%s	' "$f"; grep -c 'slots_child_port_unavailable' "$f"; done
grep -h 'slots_child_port_unavailable' <window files>   # attribute each by model=
```

### Step 5 — verdict rule

**GREEN** ⇔ chat-model router-responder `/slots` 500s = 0 **and** chat-model
fallback delta = 0 (counter **and** warning lines). Embed-model
(`mxbai-embed`) occurrences are reported separately and file a linked bug
(`discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`) without ever making the verdict RED.
Any other positive chat-model count ⇒ **RED**: name the model/responder and
file the linked bug. Report router/child 200/400 counts and the `slots_stale`
share alongside either way (AC2/AC3).

### Step 6 — evidence comment (AC5)

One comment recording: window start/end; `date -u` at run time; pid + `lstart`
+ uptime; the raw `/metrics` line(s); both per-file triage outputs verbatim;
the `proxy.log` file set with each file's observed first/last timestamp; the
dedupe/overlap rule applied; the counts; the `slots_stale` primary and
active-prefill figures; the "llama-server lines are timestamp-free ⇒ ±12 h
boundary approximation" caveat; the missed-baseline limitation; the verdict;
and any linked bug id.

AC7 and AC8 are code-change boilerplate on a measurement item — see the OPEN
QUESTION in the Appendix for the interpretation used.

## Existing state (evidence gathered at intake, 2026-10-26T23:36Z)

- **Fix is deployed.** Proxy pid 3482545 restarted 2026-10-26T21:01:42Z
  (after fix commits `f58e8964` 2026-10-26T12:51Z and `189864fc`
  2026-10-26T13:00Z, both on `dev`). Blocking item LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF is
  `completed`/`in_review`. _(Superseded 2026-10-27T10:16:11Z: pid 3482545 was
  replaced by pid **3791954**, still running at planning time. Both fix commits
  are ancestors of `dev`. The restart predates the window, so the window is
  restart-free.)_
- **Early signal the chat path is fixed.** Live 90 s spot check at
  23:36Z: 78 model-responder `/slots` events, **0** router-responder `/slots`
  events, 0 HTTP 500s.
- **Residual fallbacks exist post-fix.** `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  is already **4** since the 21:01:42Z restart, and one throttled
  `slots_child_port_unavailable` WARNING was logged at **21:01:46Z** for
  `model=mxbai-embed` (the embedding child). The current `llama-server.log`
  also still holds ~4 router-responder `/slots` lines in its last ~25 min.
  Consequence: AC4's "one occurrence fails" will very likely trip on
  restart/embed transients — resolved as Q2 option (b).
- **Rotation breaks the single-file method.** `llama-server.log` is rotated
  in-process (`rotate_llama_logs(keep=15)`, numeric `llama-server.N.log`) and
  by the `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy` safety net (daily, `copytruncate`,
  `dateext` → `llama-server.log-YYYY-MM-DD`). `proxy.log` self-rotates every
  6 h (`proxy.log.YYYY-MM-DD_HH`). A 24 h window therefore spans several
  files, and llama-server access lines carry **no timestamps**
  (`scripts/slots_500_triage.py` documents this: "no timestamps in
  llama-server logs; the corpus is per-file"). A single-file grep cannot
  cover the window — resolved at intake as Q1 option (a), hybrid.
- **Cumulative figures today** (`--llama-file 'llama-server.log'`, whole
  file, spans more than one day and predates the fixed restart):
  router 200 = 38,369; router 400 = 452; router 500 = 2,753; model 200 /
  child 200 = 68,610 + 8. Non-zero router 200s show that **direct LAN clients
  poll the router** legitimately, so raw router counts are not pure
  proxy-fallback evidence.
- **`slots_stale` alive in the current `proxy.log`**: 2,019 false / 1,952 true
  (49 % true) since the current file began — usable as an intermediate
  reference, not the window figure.
- **No existing windowed tool.** `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` classifies by
  responder/status and supports `--llama-file <glob>`, but has no
  `--since/--until`; window scoping is a manual file-set decision.

## Desired change

No product code change: this item is a **measurement and evidence** task. Its
"change" is a recorded, reproducible verdict (counts, commands, window
timestamps, and either a green pass or a new linked bug when red).

**Verdict rule (agreed):** GREEN = windowed chat-model router-responder
`/slots` 500s are 0 **and** the chat-model fallback delta is 0, with router and
child 200/400 counts and the `slots_stale` share reported alongside. RED = any
positive chat-model count; a RED verdict must name the model/responder and
create a linked bug item (`discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`). Embed-model
fallbacks never make the verdict RED — they raise a linked bug instead.

## Constraints

- Window must be a full 24 h with the fixed proxy running; restarts inside the
  window must be detected and reported (they reset counters).
- No production restart, no config change, and no code change is needed for the
  measurement itself (`start-proxy` must not be invoked unless the proxy dies).
- llama-server logs are timestamp-free → any time attribution is per-file and
  approximate; this limitation must be stated in the recorded comment, never
  silently smoothed over.
- If the verdict is red, a new bug item is created (linked
  `discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`); LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF is never silently
  reopened.
- Measurement must not perturb the proxy: read-only log greps plus a single
  `/metrics` scrape at start and end.
- **Execution gate (recorded at planning, 2026-10-28T04:40Z):** the window
  closes at **2026-10-28T12:00Z**; a run started earlier measures a partial
  window and must not be used as the AC evidence. Assignee `Map` is the
  scheduling hold — clear it at/after 2026-10-28T12:00Z to release the item.

## Key Files

- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` — existing responder/status classifier; needs a windowed (file-set) invocation or a documented file-selection recipe.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_discover_local_child_port`, `_resolve_local_slots_target`, `_warn_child_port_fallback` (emits `slots_child_port_unavailable`; throttled).
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` — `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` counter (exact, reset on restart).
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — `rotate_llama_logs(keep=15)` in-process numeric rotation (file boundaries = restarts).
- `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy` — daily `copytruncate`/`dateext` safety net for both log families.
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log` (+ `llama-server.N.log`, `llama-server.log-YYYY-MM-DD`) — router vs child `/slots` access lines.
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` (+ `proxy.log.YYYY-MM-DD_HH`) — `slots_stale`, `status_request`, `slots_child_port_unavailable`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (high): verdict goes red on embed-model transients.** Post-fix
  counter already 4 with one `mxbai-embed` warning in ~2.5 h of uptime; a
  literal AC4 makes the window almost certainly red for a cause that is not
  the busy-child 500 storm. **Resolved (Q2b):** embed fallbacks are reported
  separately and never make the verdict RED; a linked bug is filed instead.
- **Risk (medium): coverage gap.** If a rotation/restart lands mid-window, the
  single-file greps under-report. **Resolved (Q1a):** counter delta plus
  file-set aggregation, restart-aware (AC6).
- **Risk (medium): attribution.** Direct LAN clients polling the router
  produce router 200/400/500s that are not proxy-fallback symptoms; without
  source attribution the check can be red for unrelated noise. **Mitigation
  (agreed):** the fallback counter is the primary chat-path signal; raw router
  counts are reported for masquerade detection only, with the limitation
  stated in the recorded comment.
- **Risk (low): timing slip.** The 12:00Z window needs an agent at both ends;
  a late start truncates the window. Mitigation: snapshot first, then wait.
- **Assumption:** "the fix is deployed" means proxy pid started after
  `189864fc`; re-verify pid start time at window start rather than trusting
  this brief.
- **Scope-creep guard:** a reusable windowed measurement script (e.g.
  `--since/--until` on `slots_500_triage.py`) is a **separate follow-up item**,
  not part of this measurement.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF** — Residual router-proxied `/slots` 500s: audit
  remaining call sites and enforce direct child-port polling (completed; the
  fix under test here).
- **LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8** — Router `/slots` HTTP 400s: `?model=` resolution
  path (86 residual router 400 responses) — sibling split, shares AC2's 400
  reporting.
- **LP-0MTCMEV1G0022A35** — `/slots` 500-storm triage tooling
  (`scripts/slots_500_triage.py`), reused here.
- **LP-0MTIHZ8M5005ZAU8** — earlier (inert) direct-child fix; historical
  context for why the rotation-proof signal was needed.
- **LP-0MTDGBRPU003Z7KU** — 5–7 s router-proxied slot-poll latency measurement
  (the latency symptom of the same defect).
- Automated find-related report: work items LP-0MQYEY34L000H3O8 (ui.py
  `_extract_router_model_ids` NameError), LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P (proxy logger
  output), LP-0MQ6EGGJ6002JHZX (single-model mode) — same log/proxy surface,
  no AC overlap.

## Interview decisions (resolved)

- **Q1 = (a) Hybrid window scoping.** Fallback-counter delta from `/metrics` at
  window start/end (exact, restart-aware) + `scripts/slots_500_triage.py`
  counts summed across every `llama-server*.log` file whose mtime falls in the
  window, reported per-file with the "llama-server lines are timestamp-free →
  approximate attribution" caveat. No code change; a `--since/--until` upgrade
  to the triage CLI stays a separate follow-up item.
- **Q2 = (b) Chat-model zero tolerance, embed reported separately.** `Qwen3`
  path: zero router-responder 500s and zero fallbacks. `mxbai-embed` fallbacks
  are a non-blocking observation and spawn a linked bug at window end if any
  occur.
- **Q3 = (a) All `status_request` polls as the primary `slots_stale`
  denominator**, with the active-prefill subset as a secondary figure.

Source: producer reply "As recommended" (2026-10-27T00:48Z, accepting the three
recommended options in comment LP-C0MVPWPEKW004SSKP).

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-28T04:40Z — planning session (Map).** Effort/risk pre-check
  returned `skip` (Extra Small / Low), so the item was reviewed rather than
  decomposed; no child items were created (single measurement slice, one
  vertical pass through evidence → verdict → record). Changes made: verified
  window state block added to the Summary; "Execution plan" added with the
  exact commands, file-set derivation and dedupe rule; the missed 12:00Z
  baseline snapshot documented with the monotonic-counter reconstruction (AC5)
  and the superset-bound argument (AC1/AC2); the 2026-10-28T12:00Z execution
  gate added to Constraints; the superseded intake pid annotated in "Existing
  state"; one non-blocking OPEN QUESTION added for AC7/AC8. Six review stages
  run; AC coverage review returned `proceed` (leaf item, no children).
  Effort/risk reused from intake (Extra Small / Low, score 2/25) — no scope
  change to re-estimate.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION (plan, 2026-10-28T04:40Z)** — AC7 ("all related
  documentation updated … README, wiki or docs site entries") and AC8 ("full
  project test suite must pass with the new changes") read as code-change
  boilerplate, while "Desired change" states explicitly that this item makes
  **no product code change**. Working assumption used by the plan (does not
  block execution): AC7 is satisfied by the recorded measurement evidence (plus
  any doc touched if the verdict spawns a follow-up) and AC8 is satisfied by
  the standard full-suite gate (`/skill:test`) on any change this item
  produces — which is none. Directed to: producer. Why it matters: if a doc
  note (e.g. a measured-results entry under `docs/`) or an actual suite run is
  intended as part of this item's evidence, the execution plan needs one more
  step. Not blocking: the measurement and verdict are unaffected.

- Q1 "How should the window be scoped across rotated logs?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-10-27T00:48Z): option (a), hybrid** — counter delta + per-file
  triage counts across the window's file set, caveat documented. Source:
  interactive reply "As recommended" (comment LP-C0MVPWPEKW004SSKP). Research: `llama-server.log`
  has no timestamps; in-process numeric rotation (`rotate_llama_logs`,
  keep=15) and logrotate `copytruncate`/`dateext` mean a 24 h window spans
  several files; `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` supports `--llama-file` globs
  but no time window; `proxy.log` is timestamped and its
  `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` counter is exact but resets on
  restart.
- Q2 "How strict is the zero-tolerance rule?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-10-27T00:48Z): option (b)** — chat-model zero tolerance; embed-model
  fallbacks reported separately as non-blocking with a linked bug if present.
  Source: interactive reply "As recommended". Research:
  post-restart counter = 4 fallbacks
  (`no_child_port_router_mode`), 1 throttled `slots_child_port_unavailable`
  WARNING at 2026-10-26T21:01:46Z for `model=mxbai-embed`; 8
  `proxying request to model mxbai-embed` lines exist in the current log, so
  embed discovery signal is sparse rather than absent.
- Q3 "What exactly is the AC3 `slots_stale` denominator?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-10-27T00:48Z): option (a)** — all `status_request` polls as
  primary, active-prefill subset secondary. Source: interactive reply "As
  recommended".
  Research: parent intake recorded the pre-fix baseline as 579/899 *all*
  `status_request` polls in the 2026-10-26 file; `status_request` lines expose
  both `active_query` and `local_active_query`, so an active-prefill subset is
  derivable.

## Producer acceptance (2026-10-30)

Producer decision recorded after the measurement run (commit `dc410fce`,
verdict RED):

- **AC1 and AC4 are accepted as measured-not-met.** Both are outcome criteria
  on the production system ("router-responder `/slots` 500s = 0",
  "chat-model fallback delta = 0") that this measurement item cannot satisfy
  by further measurement work. They are accepted as an honest RED outcome, not
  waived: the AC text above is unchanged.
- **Verdict RED stands** as the deliverable of this item: the fix is a large
  improvement (router 500s 2,753 -> 128 on the first full post-fix day, ~95 %
  down; `slots_stale` 64.4 % -> 31.4 %; slot polling essentially all direct)
  but not the zero-tolerance target.
- **Remediation is tracked in two linked bugs** (both
  `discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`, queued open): `LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0`
  (high, the proxy `/health` reachability probe polls the router `/slots`, the
  residual 500 source) and `LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K` (medium, chat-model
  child-port fallback for an unloaded local model, `gpt120`).
- **AC2, AC3, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8 are met** (evidence comment
  `LP-C0MVVCZNZ3004F0QJ`; docs `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` section
  "Post-fix 24 h window verification" plus

discovered-from:LP-0MVOHRLPB0086Q5T

Found while fixing the Grafana GPU memory panel (LP-0MVOHRLPB0086Q5T).

## Problem

Two documents still point readers at monitoring artefacts that no longer exist on
this host:

1. `proxy/README.md` § Alerting Rules (≈ line 2895) documents a "Llama memory"
   alert "Warning at 75% of 90GB; critical at 90GB — `monitoring/llama_memory_alerts.yaml`".
   That rule file was deleted in LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48 (it compared
   `llama_process_rss_bytes`, which the proxy publishes as 0).
2. `docs/gpu-offload-verification.md` § 6 tells readers to monitor
   `rocm_vram_usage_bytes` and `rocm_device_temperature_celsius` after enabling
   offload. No exporter publishes those series (amd/rocm-exporter has no release
   artefacts); the real signals are `gpu_gtt_used_bytes`,
   `node_hwmon_power_average_watt{chip_name="amdgpu"}` and the GTT memory alerts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `proxy/README.md` names only alert rule files that exist under `monitoring/`
   and describes thresholds that match those files (verify: every
   `monitoring/*.yaml` path mentioned in the README exists).
2. `docs/gpu-offload-verification.md` § 6 points at series that are actually
   published (GTT memory + power draw) and no longer names `rocm_vram_*`.
3. A test guards both references (no stale rule-file path, no `rocm_*` series
   name in monitoring documentation).
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Goal
